name: space
title: Disk Space
description: What is taking the space: a root (home, a volume, any folder) scanned into a tree, drawn as a zoomable treemap of boxes inside boxes (Enter zooms in, Backspace out, the arrows walk the boxes), the same children as rows beside it, the biggest files and folders as lists, and cleanup suggestions (caches, stale node_modules and target folders, Xcode's DerivedData, old downloads, the Trash) with their sizes. Mark boxes and trash them together; every delete goes to the Trash after a confirm. Scans persist compactly, so reopening is instant and Rescan is explicit.
author: pal

settings.label: Sizes
settings.description: What the boxes and rows measure: the blocks a file takes on disk (what deleting it frees; sparse and compressed files are small), or its apparent length.

settings.label: Colour boxes by
settings.description: The kind of file (folder, image, video, code, archive, ...), or the place among the siblings with the nested boxes in their parent's hue (the DaisyDisk ring). `c` in the map flips it.

settings.label: Cross into other volumes
settings.text: Count folders on other file systems (mounted disks, images) under the root
settings.description: Off, a scan stays on the root's volume, so a scan of Macintosh HD does not walk every mounted disk. macOS firmlinks (/Users, /Applications on the Data volume) are always crossed.

settings.label: Largest lists
settings.description: How many rows Largest Files and Largest Folders show.

settings.label: Stale after
settings.description: Cleanup Suggestions count a node_modules or target folder, and a download, as stale past this age.

store.tagline: Big file finder and cleanup: a zoomable treemap of what fills the disk
features: A treemap of boxes inside boxes, squarified so they stay near square, area by size: Enter zooms into a folder, Backspace out, the arrows walk the boxes by position, Tab by size
Scans are a parallel Bun walk (a million-file home in 7 s, four times du), drawn live as they run; sizes on disk or apparent, hard links once, other volumes skipped, symlinks never followed
Colour by kind or by depth; the same children as rows beside the board with size, share and count; a footer line about the focused box
Mark boxes with `m` and trash them together: the marked total in the header, one confirm, everything to the Trash (never a silent delete)
Largest Files and Largest Folders under any scanned root, with Quick Look, reveal, open, copy path and a multi-select trash
Cleanup Suggestions: user caches, package caches, Xcode's DerivedData, stale node_modules and target folders, old downloads, the Trash, each with its size and a confirmed action
Scans persist compactly (the biggest nodes), so reopening is instant; Rescan is explicit; a zoom into a folder the saved scan cut rescans just that folder
permissions: Full Disk Access, for ~/Library/Mail and the like (unreadable folders are counted and named)
